title: OSHA Gas Can Checklist (29 CFR 1926.152)
subtitle: For walk-through checks of flammable liquid containers, storage, dispensing and refueling areas on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For each Defect, note the location and report it to the supervisor responsible for the area; this reporting step is a site practice, not a step taken from the regulation text.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Gas cans and containers
items: Flammable liquids are held only in approved containers or portable tanks; none in unapproved jugs or buckets

Liquids handled and used in quantities of 5 gallons or less are in approved safety cans or DOT-approved containers; the permitted alternatives are a highly viscid liquid in its original shipping container, or one gallon or less in the original container
Category 1–3 liquid containers are closed whenever not actually in use
No standing leaks or spilled liquid; spill material has been removed and disposed of safely

sections.title: Storage areas and extinguishers
items: No flammable liquids stored in exits, on stairways or in walkways people normally use
No more than 25 gallons in the room outside an approved storage cabinet
Cabinet carries conspicuous lettering reading "Flammable-Keep Away from Open Flames"
Each cabinet holds no more than 60 gallons of Category 1–3 liquids or 120 gallons of Category 4
Three cabinets or fewer in the storage area
Outdoor container piles are at least 20 feet from buildings, 5 feet apart and no larger than 1,100 gallons each
No weeds, debris or unneeded combustible material in the outdoor storage area
20-B or greater unit mounted outside the door of a room holding over 60 gallons, within 10 feet of the opening
20-B or greater unit placed 25 to 75 feet from the outdoor storage area

sections.title: Dispensing, transfer and point of use
items: Areas transferring more than 5 gallons at one time are 25 feet from other operations or behind 1-hour fire-resistant construction
Bonding connection in place between containers before any Category 1–3 liquid is transferred
Liquid is moved by closed piping, from safety cans, by a top-drawing device, or by gravity or pump through an approved self-closing valve; no air pressure on containers
Dispensing unit is shielded from impact by vehicles and equipment
No open flames, welding or other ignition sources within 50 feet of where Category 1–3 liquids are used, or a greater clearance where conditions warrant it
Tank truck or fuel-dispensing vehicle carries a 20-B:C or greater extinguisher

sections.title: Service and refueling areas
items: Dispensing hose is an approved type
Approved automatic-closing nozzle with no latch-open device fitted
Clearly identified, easily reached switch away from the dispensers cuts power to all of them
Nobody smoking and no open flames in fueling, receiving or dispensing areas
Conspicuous, legible no-smoking signs posted at the fueling area
Equipment motors are shut off throughout fueling
20-B:C or greater unit within 75 feet of every pump, dispenser, underground fill pipe opening and lubrication or service area

references: 29 CFR 1926.152: Flammable liquids (Part 1926 Subpart F, Fire Protection and Prevention)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
